title: HELIOS-B: A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy
off: HELIOS-B: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Multicenter Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy (ATTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy)
summary: This study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of vutrisiran 25 mg administered subcutaneously (SC) once every 3 months (q3M) compared to placebo in participants with ATTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Has a documented diagnosis of transthyretin (ATTR) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy, classified as either hereditary ATTR (hATTR) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy or wild-type ATTR (wtATTR) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy meeting pre-specified diagnostic criteria
* Has medical history of heart failure (HF) with at least 1 prior hospitalization for HF OR clinical evidence of HF

Exclusion Criteria:

* Has known primary amyloidosis or leptomeningeal amyloidosis
* Has New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class IV heart failure
* Has NYHA Class III heart failure AND is at high risk based on pre-specified criteria
* Has a polyneuropathy disability (PND) Score IIIa, IIIb, or IV at the Screening visit
* Has estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) \<30 mL/min/1.73 m\^2
* Has received prior TTR-lowering treatment
* Has other non-TTR cardiomyopathy, hypertensive cardiomyopathy, cardiomyopathy due to valvular heart disease, or cardiomyopathy due to ischemic heart disease

arms.d: Participants received vutrisiran 25 milligrams (mg) administered subcutaneously (SC) once every 3 months (q3M) during the 36-month double-blind (DB) period. After the DB period, participants continue receiving vutrisiran, 25 mg, SC injection, q3M for up to 24 months in the open-label treatment extension (OLE) period.

Participants received vutrisiran matching placebo administered SC q3M during the 36-month DB period. After the DB period, participants receive vutrisiran, 25 mg, SC injection, q3M for up to 24 months in the OLE period.

abstracts:
Garcia-Pavia P, Witteles R, Morbach C, Delgado D, Kitaoka H, Maurer MS, et al. Long-Term Impact of Vutrisiran in Patients With TTR Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy: 1-Year Efficacy and Safety Outcomes From the HELIOS-B Open-Label Extension. Circulation. 2026. doi: 10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.126.080735
BACKGROUND: In HELIOS-B (A Study to Evaluate Vutrisiran in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy), vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause mortality (ACM) and recurrent cardiovascular events and slowed disease progression measures versus placebo in patients with TTR (transthyretin) amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy after 33 to 36 months. We report the long-term efficacy and safety of vutrisiran from an ongoing open-label extension of HELIOS-B.
METHODS: Patients who completed HELIOS-B could enroll in the open-label extension, continuing with vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (continuous vutrisiran) or, if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran 25 mg every 3 months (placebo/vutrisiran). Prespecified end points assessed in the open-label extension are the composite of ACM and cardiovascular events, ACM, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score, New York Heart Association class, and NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide) and troponin I levels. Outcomes were assessed through month 48 in this analysis.
RESULTS: Of 654 participants in HELIOS-B (vutrisiran, n=326; placebo, n=328), 478 completed double-blind treatment and 466 (vutrisiran, n=243; placebo, n=223) entered the open-label extension. In the continuous vutrisiran group, the risk of first cardiovascular event or ACM was reduced by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.51, 0.79]; P=0.0001) and ACM by 37% (hazard ratio, 0.63 [95% CI, 0.46, 0.84]; P=0.0023) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Through month 48, patients in the continuous vutrisiran group had preserved health status and quality of life per Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Overall Summary score (least squares mean difference, 9.0 [95% CI, 5.3, 12.6]; P<0.0001) and more patients had improved or stable New York Heart Association class (odds ratio, 1.6 [95% CI, 1.1, 2.2]; P=0.0084) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Benefits in the continuous vutrisiran group were maintained for NT-proBNP and troponin I levels (adjusted geometric mean fold change ratios, 0.66 [95% CI, 0.58, 0.74]; P<0.0001; and 0.71 [95% CI, 0.64, 0.79]; P<0.0001, respectively) versus the placebo/vutrisiran group. Similar benefits were observed in the vutrisiran monotherapy population. No new safety signals were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term vutrisiran resulted in clinically meaningful benefits across mortality, cardiovascular events, cardiac biomarkers, functional status, and quality of life in patients with TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy through month 48. Patients initially treated with vutrisiran had better outcomes than those first receiving placebo, highlighting the importance of early diagnosis and treatment in TTR amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy.

Cuddy SAM, Griffin JM, Tang WHW, Lairez O, Morbach C, Cappelli F, et al. Continuous Vutrisiran Reduces Cardiovascular Events and Hospitalizations in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy in the HELIOS-B One-Year Open Label Extension. J Card Fail. 2026. doi: 10.1016/j.cardfail.2026.09.017
BACKGROUND: Vutrisiran significantly reduced the risk of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular (CV) events vs placebo in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in the phase 3 HELIOS-B study (NCT04153149). Here, we report the long-term impact of vutrisiran on hospitalizations and urgent heart failure (HF) visits from the ongoing HELIOS-B open-label extension (OLE).
METHODS: In HELIOS-B, patients received vutrisiran 25 mg or placebo every 3 months over a 33-36-month double-blind period, followed by a 24-month OLE continuing with vutrisiran (continuous treatment), or if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran (delayed treatment). Hospitalizations and urgent HF visits were analyzed through 48 months (12 months of the OLE) in the overall and monotherapy (not receiving tafamidis at baseline) populations, and the baseline tafamidis subgroup.
RESULTS: Of 654 participants, 466 entered the OLE. Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause hospitalizations vs delayed treatment in the overall population (relative rate ratio [RRR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.82, P<0.001) and the monotherapy population (RRR 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.72, P<0.001). Continuous vutrisiran also significantly reduced the risk of CV hospitalizations, HF hospitalizations, and non-CV hospitalizations vs delayed vutrisiran in the overall and monotherapy populations, and urgent HF visits in the overall population and baseline tafamidis subgroup.
CONCLUSIONS: Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of CV events and hospitalizations relative to patients originally randomized to placebo in HELIOS-B. Many treatment effects were of greater magnitude at 48 months vs 36 months with continuous vutrisiran, highlighting the benefits of earlier diagnosis and treatment.

IMPORTANCE: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is common among patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) and portends worse prognosis. The effects of vutrisiran on RV function remain incompletely characterized.
OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence and prognostic importance of RV dysfunction in ATTR-CM, and to evaluate the effect of vutrisiran on RV function.

x.titre: Vutrisiran contre placebo dans la cardiomyopathie amyloïde à transthyrétine
x.question: Le vutrisiran réduit-il la mortalité toutes causes et les événements cardiovasculaires récurrents dans l'amylose cardiaque à transthyrétine ?
x.contexte:
L'amylose cardiaque à transthyrétine (ATTR-CM), héréditaire ou sauvage, est une cause importante d'insuffisance cardiaque à fraction d'éjection préservée chez le sujet âgé. Elle évolue avec une surcharge amyloïde progressive du myocarde et un risque élevé d'hospitalisation et de décès. Au moment de la conception de l'étude, le tafamidis était le seul traitement ayant montré un bénéfice sur la mortalité.

Le vutrisiran est un ARN interférent à action hépatique, qui réduit la production de TTR variante et sauvage. Il est administré par voie sous-cutanée tous les 3 mois. HELIOS-B est une étude de phase 3 randomisée, en double aveugle, contre placebo, chez environ 650 patients. Elle compare le vutrisiran 25 mg au placebo pendant 36 mois, en autorisant un traitement de fond de l'insuffisance cardiaque et un stabilisateur de la TTR. Les patients sous placebo passent au vutrisiran en extension ouverte de 24 mois. Le promoteur est Alnylam Pharmaceuticals.
x.interet: L'étude teste un traitement de silencing de la TTR dans l'ATTR-CM, avec un critère clinique de morbi-mortalité. Son analyse en sous-groupe sous monothérapie précise la place du vutrisiran en l'absence de stabilisateur.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 85 ans atteints d'amylose cardiaque à transthyrétine, héréditaire ou sauvage, avec insuffisance cardiaque.
inclusion: Diagnostic documenté d'ATTR avec cardiomyopathie (hATTR ou wtATTR), selon des critères prédéfinis
Antécédent d'insuffisance cardiaque avec au moins une hospitalisation, ou signes cliniques d'insuffisance cardiaque
exclusion: Amylose primaire (AL) ou amylose leptoméningée connue
Insuffisance cardiaque NYHA IV, ou NYHA III avec risque élevé selon des critères prédéfinis
Handicap lié à la polyneuropathie (score PND IIIa, IIIb ou IV)
Autre cardiopathie non liée à la TTR (hypertensive, valvulaire, ischémique)

bras.traitement: Vutrisiran 25 mg SC tous les 3 mois pendant 36 mois en double aveugle, puis jusqu'à 24 mois en extension ouverte
Placebo SC tous les 3 mois pendant 36 mois, puis vutrisiran 25 mg tous les 3 mois jusqu'à 24 mois en extension ouverte

x.duree: 36 mois en double aveugle, puis jusqu'à 24 mois d'extension ouverte
x.critere: Critère composite de la mortalité toutes causes et des événements cardiovasculaires récurrents (hospitalisations cardiovasculaires et consultations urgentes pour insuffisance cardiaque), dans la population globale et dans le sous-groupe sous monothérapie, jusqu'à 36 mois.
x.resultats: Sur le critère composite principal (mortalité toutes causes et événements cardiovasculaires récurrents, hospitalisations CV et consultations urgentes pour insuffisance cardiaque), un événement est survenu chez 125 patients sous vutrisiran (n = 326) contre 159 sous placebo (n = 328) à 36 mois au plus. Le hazard ratio est de 0,718 (IC 95 % 0,555 à 0,929 ; p = 0,0118). Dans le sous-groupe en monothérapie par vutrisiran, le hazard ratio est de 0,672 (IC 95 % 0,487 à 0,929 ; p = 0,0162), avec 76 patients concernés sur 196 contre 105 sur 199 sous placebo. Des événements indésirables graves ont été rapportés chez 201 patients sous vutrisiran et 220 sous placebo, et 49 décès sous vutrisiran contre 63 sous placebo. Le registre ne fournit pas de conclusion rédigée des auteurs ; les résultats vont dans le sens d'un bénéfice du vutrisiran.
